messages:
sam: quick flag, noticed host CPU p95 up ~8% on tiny streaming chats after yesterday's runtime kernel selector rollout. traces point at small writes + HPACK overhead.

lucy: saw it too. flamegraph: https://internal-gists/redwood/fg-437001 — big stacks in http2::encode_hpack and proxy::flush_buffer. :confused:

omar: GPUs steady. host syscall rate doubled for many clients doing 50-200B chunks. looks like writev per-mini-frame.

sam: reproducer i used (python):
```python
import requests
for _ in range(500):
    r = requests.post('https://ingress.redwood/api/v1/stream', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer x'}, data='{"input":"hi"}', stream=True)
    for c in r.iter_content(chunk_size=64):
        pass
```
this creates lots of tiny frames.

nora: infra note: after the kernel swap the TCP socket write path went from batching at kernel hint -> direct small writes because kernel chosen avoided coalesce prep. also http2 SETTINGS on the proxy are default, including max_frame_size=16384.

lucy: theory: kernel_select now prefers a minimal-alloc short-path for seq_len<40 which skips the buffer-assemble that used to pack multiple chunks into a single writev. result: more HPACK encoding cycles and more syscalls.

omar: profiling data:
- http2::encode_hpack: +35% cycles
- syscall::writev count: x2
- kvcache.eviction.rate: +18% on shard-7 under this load

sam: interesting re: kvcache  the preparse code touches KV to check prefix normalization for each chunk; if chunks are more numerous, we thrash the shard lock and evict more.

lucy: quick mitigation candidates: (A) proxy-level micro-batching: coalesce up to 1024 bytes or 6ms; (B) adjust kernel selection predicate to re-enable coalesce for short seqs when writev hot; (C) reuse HPACK encoder instance per-connection to reduce allocs.

nora: rolling (A) & (C) as a canary now. config: \"proxy.coalesce_ms\": 6, \"proxy.coalesce_bytes\": 1024, \"http2.hpack_reuse\": true.

omar: i'll instrument per-connection writev_count and per-shard eviction metrics + post canary graphs.

sam: small change note for (B): patch idea:
```diff
- if (seq_len < 40) return ShortNoCoalesce();
+ if (seq_len < 40 && !telemetry.writev_rate_high(conn)) return ShortNoCoalesce();
```
we can gate by runtime telemetry.

lucy: agree. longer-term: add a kernel scoring pass that includes host-side IO penalty as a factor. kernsel_score += writev_penalty(conn.writev_rate);

triage-bot: canary metrics posted: host p95 CPU down ~6.5%, writev_count dropped ~48%, per-shard kvcache evictions down ~13%. (auto-post)

omar: promising. next: run latency SLO smoke to ensure no user-visible regressions (esp 99th). also check HTTP/2 flow control interactions after coalesce.

nora: infra ticket INF-2033 created for canary and logs attached.
sam: owners: proxy coalesce/HPACK reuse -> nora, telemetry + eviction counters -> omar, kernel scoring follow-up -> lucy.

lucy: i'll prototype host-penalty knob in kernel selector and run a kernel-sweep testbed.

omar: adding unit test in preparse harness that simulates 1000 tiny chunk clients to catch future regressions.

sam: thanks. update in ~3h after extended canary. :thumbsup:
